_gatesNote.description: Gates are NOT defined in workflows.yaml. bubbles/registry/gates.yaml is the sole definition surface (IMP-042 SCOPE-13); the generated copy that used to live here was deleted, so `gates` is no longer required. The `gates` shape below is retained so a downstream tree still carrying the pre-removal copy validates rather than erroring during upgrade.

classification.description: IMP-027 SCOPE-2c. modelCompensation gates exist because models are unreliable and SHOULD retire as models improve; businessInvariant gates encode a rule that holds regardless of executor and never retire; hybrid is genuinely both. Without this split there is no way to answer which gates could ever be turned off.

retireWhen.description: IMP-027 SCOPE-11. The measurement that would have to hold before this modelCompensation gate could be retired: the named metric must stay below threshold across `window` independent runs on a model of at least minTier. Legal ONLY on modelCompensation gates - businessInvariant and hybrid gates encode a rule that holds regardless of executor and never retire. Recording the criterion does NOT retire anything: no harness yet drives a model across the golden-task corpus to produce these rates, so every criterion is currently unmet on its evidence precondition. Retirement is a human edit backed by that measurement, never a tool inference.

minTier.description: Lowest model tier at which measuring this gate's retirement is even worth doing.

metric.description: The observed failure rate that must fall below threshold. Named after the failure this gate prevents, so the measurement is specific to the gate rather than a generic quality score.

threshold.description: Rate in (0,1), exclusive. Scales with blast radius: a false completion claim is unrecoverable because it is believed rather than noticed, so those gates carry tighter bounds than formatting gates.

window.description: Number of independent runs the rate must hold across. A single clean run is not evidence.

enforcedBy.description: IMP-027 SCOPE-2a. Declares the surface(s) that actually enforce this gate, so docs/generated/gate-coverage-map.md is derived from a declaration instead of inferred by grepping gate IDs out of scripts. 'mode-required' means a mode demands the gate but no dedicated mechanical enforcer implements it; 'unbound' means no enforcement surface exists and is deliberately left visible rather than hidden behind a plausible-looking binding.

since.description: IMP-036 SCOPE-8. Framework version in which this gate first appeared, derived from git history by gate-vintage-annotate.sh. A spec delivered before this version was never measured against this gate, so a sweep that reopens it is re-litigating closed work under rules that did not exist. Consumed by gate-vintage-guard.sh, which reports the mismatch and never auto-excuses it.

sinceDate.description: IMP-036 SCOPE-8. ISO date of the commit that introduced this gate. Compared against a spec's first-commit date because specs record dates, not framework versions.
